Fix: Create config directory before writing

Ensures the destination directory exists before writing the config file.

When setting up the user config file from a template, the code did not
ensure that the destination directory existed before attempting to write
the file. This would cause an error if the directory did not exist,
which is the case for a new user.

This change adds a call to `CommonUtils.EnsurePath` to create the
directory if it does not exist.

Update __init__.py

Rewrite of the print_table output method.

This is in response to the need for greater control over column widths and other formatting options.

The method is rewritten to directly output an HTML table instead of the original markdown approach. It introduces more CSS options through classes. This in turn allows different formatting options to be specified for each table in the same output window (which was limited in the original).

The new funcionality can be optionally called with new kwargs. If these are not specified, the original functionality of the old print_table is maintained. 

It adds some data validation to check that arguments of type list are of the same length.

Finally, this contribution should male it easier to later implement HTML colspan options to make more flexible tables.

feat: add rocket_mode support to C# loader

Read the rocket_mode INI key in PyRevitConfig and expose it via a new
RocketMode property, matching the existing LoadBeta/NewLoader pattern.

UIManagerService picks up the value at startup and on every BuildUI
(so a reload applies the change without restarting Revit) and skips the
parallel icon pre-load when rocket mode is active, reducing startup
latency in line with the IPY loader behaviour.

A unit test (TestRocketModeConfigFromIni) covers default, explicit
true/false, case-insensitive, and round-trip write/read cases.

feat: populate AppDomain session environment dictionary (FIX 1)

The C# loader never seeded the PYREVITEnvVarsDict AppDomain key, so all
pyrevit.sessioninfo / telemetry / logger APIs in scripts were crashing
with NullReferenceException when EnvDictionary() tried to cast null to
PythonDictionary.

Changes:
- EnvVariables.cs (Runtime): add static EnvDictionary.Seed() that
  accepts a plain Dictionary<string, object>, creates/gets the
  PythonDictionary internally, populates it, and stores it in AppDomain.
  Keeping PythonDictionary creation inside the Runtime avoids a
  compile-time IronPython reference in the loader (UseIronPython=false).

- PyRevitConfig.cs: add 12 missing config properties read from the same
  INI sections as PyRevitConsts in the CLI library:
  LoggingLevel (verbose/debug → 0/1/2), FileLogging, AutoUpdate,
  OutputStyleSheet [core]; TelemetryState, TelemetryUTCTimeStamps,
  TelemetryFilePath, TelemetryServerUrl, TelemetryIncludeHooks,
  AppTelemetryState, AppTelemetryServerUrl, AppTelemetryEventFlags
  [telemetry].

- EnvDictionarySeeder.cs (new): builds the values dict from PyRevitConfig
  and UIApplication, resolves pyRevit version from the version file and
  IronPython version from the engine DLL, then calls EnvDictionary.Seed()
  via reflection (same pattern as ScriptExecutor.Initialize/ExecuteScript).

- SessionManagerService.cs: call SeedEnvironmentDictionary() immediately
  after InitializeScriptExecutor() (which loads _runtimeAssembly) and
  before any extension startup script runs. Failure is logged as a
  warning rather than thrown to preserve graceful degradation.

- ScriptMetadataParsingTest.cs: add TestLoggingLevelConfigFromIni,
  TestTelemetryConfigFromIni, TestFileLoggingAndAutoUpdateConfigFromIni.

fix(parser): restore legacy SPECIAL_CHARS sanitization in SanitizeClassName (#3164)

The C# ExtensionParser.SanitizeClassName() replaced all non-alphanumeric chars with '_', losing information that the legacy Python cleanup_string() preserved (e.g. '-' -> 'MINUS', '.' -> 'DOT', '&' -> 'AND'). This caused UniqueId mismatches between the Python and C# loaders, breaking sessionmgr.execute_command() and Shift-Win-Click IDs for any extension directory containing special characters.

Changes:

- ExtensionParser.cs: Replaced char.IsLetterOrDigit loop with full SPECIAL_CHARS replacement table matching pyrevitlib/pyrevit/coreutils/__init__.py lines 295-344

- Includes rebuilt DLLs for both NETFX and NETCORE targets

Replace plain (, ), and / with escaped sequences \(, \), and \/ to match
the Python SPECIAL_CHARS dict which uses raw strings r'\(', r'\)', and r'\/'
that only match the literal 2-character sequences with backslashes.

Adds final validation pass to SanitizeClassName to strip any remaining
characters not valid in C# identifiers (non-ASCII, special chars not in
SPECIAL_CHARS table). Prevents assembly-load failures from invalid class
names like 'caféMINUStoolDOT'.

fix(parser): address review — match Python raw-string keys, add safety net

1. Parentheses and forward-slash now match Python 2-char raw-string sequences

   to catch Unicode or unlisted chars that would produce invalid C# identifiers

fix: prevent toolbar disappearing after reload when tabs are renamed (#3167)

Root cause: RibbonScanner registers tabs by their mutable Title property.
When a script (e.g. translation) renames tab.Title, the scanner registry
key no longer matches what the UI builder marks as touched. Cleanup then
deactivates the tab as orphaned.

Fix:
- ITabBuilder: CreateTab returns string? (renamed title if detected)
- TabBuilder: single ribbon scan — find, tag, enable, detect rename.
  Uses exact Id match via string.Equals (not substring).
- UIManagerService: HandleTab uses CreateTab return value (no redundant
  scan). Dual-marks both original and renamed Title in scanner registry.
  renamedTabTitle propagated through HandlePanel child recursion.

feat: Add Ctrl+C and Ctrl+A keyboard shortcuts to ScriptConsole output window

Fixes #1729

The pyRevit output window hosts a WebBrowser control inside a WPF
MetroWindow via WindowsFormsHost. Revit's message loop intercepts
Ctrl+C via IOleInPlaceActiveObject.TranslateAccelerator before WPF,
WinForms, IMessageFilter, or JavaScript events can see the keystroke.

This adds a Win32 low-level keyboard hook (WH_KEYBOARD_LL) that
intercepts Ctrl+C and Ctrl+A at the OS level, before Revit's
accelerator table processes them. The hook only activates when the
ScriptConsole is the active window with renderer focus, and forwards
the keystrokes to HtmlDocument.ExecCommand for native browser copy.

The hook is installed on window creation and disposed on close.

fix: resolve pyRevit/IPY version showing Unknown in output window

SeedEnvironmentDictionary() was called before _pyRevitRoot was resolved,
so EnvDictionarySeeder.Seed() received an empty string for pyRevitRoot.
Both ReadPyRevitVersion() and ReadIPYVersion() returned "Unknown" because
the repo root path was empty, skipping the version file and IronPython.dll
lookup entirely.

Fix: eagerly resolve _pyRevitRoot from _binDir inside InitializeScriptExecutor(),
which runs immediately before SeedEnvironmentDictionary() in LoadSession().
The executing assembly lives at {pyRevitRoot}/bin/, so FindPyRevitRoot(_binDir)
walks up one level and finds pyrevitlib/. If it fails (non-standard layout),
_pyRevitRoot stays null and BuildSearchPaths() retries later with the extension
directory as an additional hint.
use projectelevation instead of elevation for levels

Add debug log after FindPyRevitRoot in InitializeScriptExecutor

Log whether pyRevit root resolution succeeded or fell back to null,
making it easier to diagnose version-display issues in the output window.

Add PyRevitRootResolutionTests to verify that FindPyRevitRoot correctly
resolves the repo root from a bin/ subdirectory (via pyRevitfile marker
or pyrevitlib/ directory), and that ReadPyRevitVersion/ReadIPYVersion
return actual values (not 'Unknown') when given a valid root.

End-to-end tests replicate the exact bug scenario: without early
resolution of _pyRevitRoot in InitializeScriptExecutor(), the
SeedEnvironmentDictionary() call receives an empty string, causing
both version reads to short-circuit to 'Unknown'.

fix(adc): ADC v2027 compatibility — filesystem fallback for .NET 8

ADC v2027 (v7.8.1.11) removed the .NET 8-compatible API DLL from
FOS/AddInProcess/Civil3DOE. Both remaining API CLSsurfaces (legacy API.dll
and new API.Public.dll) were compiled against .NET Framework's unified
System.ServiceModel, making them unusable on Revit 2025/2026 (.NET 8).

Fix: three-tier fallback in adc.py
- Tier 1: Public API (future-proof for when Autodesk fixes the DLL)
- Tier 2: Legacy API (ADC v15-v17, exclusive elif to prevent AppDomain poison)
- Tier 3: Filesystem fallback (process detection + workspace dir walking)

Also restructures Keynote Manager diagnostic into safe/deep tiers to
prevent WCF AppDomain poisoning during troubleshooting.

Tested on: ADC v17.x + Revit 2024, ADC v17.x + Revit 2026,
           ADC v2027 + Revit 2024, ADC v2027 + Revit 2026.

fix: routes server Python 3 / IronPython 3.4 compatibility (#2156)

Three Python 2 APIs in the routes server silently fail under
IronPython 3.4, causing ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE for all HTTP requests:

1. self.headers.getheader() → .get()
   Python 2 mimetools.Message has .getheader(); Python 3
   http.client.HTTPMessage uses .get(). The .get() method works
   on both, so no version guard is needed.

2. sys.exc_type / sys.exc_traceback → local variables
   These were deprecated thread-local attributes in Python 2,
   removed in Python 3. Use local variables from sys.exc_info()
   instead (standard practice since Python 2.6+).

3. cgi.parse_header() → str.split(";")
   The cgi module is deprecated (Python 3.11+, removal in 3.15).
   Only the content-type value is needed here, so a simple split
   replaces the import entirely.

Also guards .clsException access in handler.py with getattr(),
since IronPython 3 may not expose this attribute on exceptions.

fix(config): prevent telemetry config escape-doubling

Three telemetry config fields (telemetry_file_dir,
telemetry_server_url, apptelemetry_server_url) accumulated JSON
escape characters geometrically on every reload, growing each
value to ~8 MB after ~22 cycles and slowing reload from ~40s to
~3 min.

Root cause: asymmetric encode/decode in
PyRevitConfigSectionParser. __setattr__ unconditionally
json.dumps-wraps the value, while __getattr__'s outer fallthrough
returns a fallback-chain-mutated string when all three json.loads
attempts fail. The mutated value gets re-encoded on the next
write, compounding on every reload via setup_telemetry() and
upgrade_user_config().

Three changes:

1. coreutils/configparser.py
   - __setattr__ adds an idempotency check that skips the write
     when the encoded value matches what's already stored.
   - __getattr__ returns the original raw bytes (not the mutated
     fallback 'value') when all decode attempts fail.

2. versionmgr/upgrade.py
   - Adds heal_bloated_telemetry_fields() to detect and reset
     bloated fields on the next reload, with a backup of the
     original config saved as <config>.bloated.<timestamp>.bak.
   - Called from upgrade_user_config() before the format-upgrade
     loop so multi-megabyte values never round-trip the loop.

3. telemetry/__init__.py
   - Adds persist=True parameter to set_telemetry_file_dir,
     set_telemetry_server_url, set_apptelemetry_server_url.
   - setup_telemetry() passes persist=False, eliminating the
     redundant round-trip read-write cycle that previously fed
     the bug. Settings GUI save path keeps default persist=True.

Verified against a real 24 MB bloated config:
- Heal correctly reduced live config from 24,580 KB -> 4 KB on
  first launch, with backup preserved.
- Steady-state reload cycles produce 0-byte size delta (Fix A
  idempotency check working as designed).
- All three affected fields reset to "" post-heal.

fix: restore module globals in execute_in_revit_context before ExternalEvent fires

When the IronPython engine clears a non-persistent script scope, or when the
cached engine for a command is the startup-script engine (same TypeId via
SessionUUID:EngineType:Extension), module references like `forms`, `revit`, and
any other split-backend module can disappear from func.__globals__ before the
ExternalEvent callback executes, causing NameError.

Snapshot all module-type globals at scheduling time and restore any that are
missing just before the function is called. Only module objects (type(v) is
type(compat)) are restored, so mutable Revit state (doc, uidoc, etc.) is never
overwritten with stale values.

fix: address reviewer concerns in execute_in_revit_context

Replace singleton func/args/kwargs slots with a queue.Queue so rapid
back-to-back calls no longer silently drop earlier invocations.

Scope globals restoration with save/patch/finally-restore so only
missing or None module names are touched and the original state is
always put back, limiting the mutation window to the call itself.

Guard restoration with `k not in g or g[k] is None` so a freshly
re-imported module between scheduling and execution is never overwritten
by the scheduling-time snapshot.

Note: types.FunctionType with non-empty closures is unsupported in
IronPython 2, so a shadow-dict approach is not viable; bounded mutation
is the safest available option.

Share single SmartButtonScriptInitializer across button-builder paths

Previously CreateButtonBuilderFactory and CreateStackBuilder each
constructed their own SmartButtonScriptInitializer, causing the
IronPython engine for SmartButtons to spin up twice per reload —
once when the standalone-button path hit its first SmartButton,
again when the stack path hit its first SmartButton.

same instance to both factories. The SmartButtonExecutor's engine
init was already idempotent; the duplication was purely upstream.

Verified on a default-ribbon reload: engine init count drops from 2
to 1, pyRevitCore BuildUI drops ~490ms, total captured reload time
drops ~1.8s (~19%).

Add sidecar file capture to LoggingHelper

When PYREVIT_CSHARP_LOG_FILE is set, every log call also appends a
timestamped line to that path. Sidesteps the C#-to-Python-FileHandler
bridge issue where mlogger calls from C# are silently dropped before
reaching runtime.log, so [PERF] markers and load-time diagnostics can
be captured reliably for analysis.

Add per-type and per-panel timing inside BuildUI

Wraps the top-of-extension foreach in BuildUI and the per-child foreach
inside HandleTab with Stopwatches, aggregating into instance fields on
UIManagerService. SessionManagerService calls EmitBuildUIPerfLines right
after the existing wrapping line so the sub-step detail is indented
under it in the log, making it obvious whether a slow extension is
dominated by one panel or spread evenly.

Add sub-step timers to ButtonPostProcessor.Process

Each Process call now records elapsed time for icon, tooltip, contextual
help, and highlight separately into Interlocked-guarded accumulators
exposed via IButtonPostProcessor.ResetAndGetStats(). UIManagerService
clears the counters at the start of each BuildUI and snapshots them at
the end so EmitBuildUIPerfLines can attribute one Post: line per
extension, isolating which of the four substeps dominates without
flooding the log with per-button lines.

Add cache hit/miss and decode-time instrumentation for icons

BitmapCache now Interlocked-counts hits and misses on each TryGet, and
IconManager.LoadBitmapSource accumulates the elapsed time of the
BitmapImage decode + EnsureProperDpi path on cache misses. Both surface
through IIconManager.ResetAndGetStats(), which UIManagerService clears
at the start of each BuildUI and snapshots at the end so
EmitBuildUIPerfLines can attribute one Icons: hits/misses/decode line
per extension - exposing whether the cache is effective and whether
icon decode is a real cost on cold load.

Add AddItem and SmartButton selfinit timing per extension

Every parentPanel.AddItem / splitBtn.AddPushButton / pdBtn.AddPushButton
call across PushButton/Split/Pulldown/Panel/Link builders now records
its elapsed time into a shared accumulator on ButtonPostProcessor, and
SmartButtonScriptInitializer wraps the IronPython __selfinit__ Invoke
in a Stopwatch. UIManagerService resets both at the start of each
BuildUI and snapshots at the end, so EmitBuildUIPerfLines can attribute
two new lines per extension - AddItem total + count and SmartButton
selfinit total + count - directly answering whether the Revit ribbon
API or SmartButton init scripts are the load-time bottleneck.

Add per-extension composition counts to BuildUI [PERF] lines

RecursivelyBuildUI now increments per-type counters (and child counts
for compound components like splits/pulldowns/stacks) as it walks each
supported component. EmitBuildUIPerfLines closes each extension's
[PERF] block with one Counts: line listing panels, push, smart, split,
pulldown, stack, etc., so a slow extension can be read in context -
3.8s across 24 push buttons reads very differently from 3.8s across
200.

Move sidecar log path to pyrevit_config.ini

LoggingHelper now reads the sidecar log path from
[core] csharp_loader_log_file in pyrevit_config.ini via
PyRevitConfig.Load(), instead of a PYREVIT_CSHARP_LOG_FILE OS env var.
Aligns with how every other user-facing loader knob (RocketMode,
LoadBeta, OutputStyleSheet, LoggingLevel) is configured - the codebase
reads no pyRevit-namespaced OS env vars elsewhere.

Make sidecar logging a boolean toggle matching filelogging

Replace the user-supplied path knob with a boolean [core] csharp_filelogging,
parallel to the existing [core] filelogging that controls runtime.log. When
enabled, LoggingHelper writes to %APPDATA%\pyRevit\{revitVersion}\pyRevit_
{revitVersion}_{pid}_csharp_loader.log - the same per-version, per-process
location convention runtime.log already uses. ServiceFactory threads
revitVersion into CreateLogger so the path can be resolved at construction.

Add per-extension parse timing to ParseInstalledExtensions

The 3-second [PERF] GetLibraryExtensions line was misleading: it timed
the lazy ParseInstalledExtensions enumeration that populates the
shared bundle parser cache (used by both GetInstalledLibraryExtensions
and GetInstalledUIExtensions), not the lib-only filter.

Wrap each ParseExtension call in ExtensionParser.ParseInstalledExtensions
with a Stopwatch and append to a process-wide accumulator that
SessionManagerService drains via ResetAndGetParseStats after
.ToList() materializes the enumerator. Emit the renamed wrapping line
[PERF] ParseAllExtensions: Nms (X ui, Y lib) plus one indented
[PERF]   parse '<bundle>': Nms line per extension sorted by elapsed
so a slow bundle is immediately visible.

Split SmartButton selfinit timing into per-stage + per-button [PERF] lines

The previous aggregate (selfinit=1512ms x3) conflated four very different
costs — IronPython engine cold-start, per-script compile, module-body
execute, and __selfinit__ invocation — making it impossible to tell which
lever to pull. Empirical data from the new split shows engine init is
~9ms (not the ~500ms that was assumed) and the dominant cost is the
first SmartButton's module-body execute (~2000ms loading the shared
pyrevit-library imports into a fresh engine).

SmartButtonExecutor now times each stage with its own Stopwatch.
Engine-init time uses a drain-on-read accumulator so reload BuildUIs
correctly report engineInit=0ms (engine survives across the session).

SmartButtonScriptInitializer caches reflection accessors to the new
executor surface, drains stats per call into a per-extension batch,
and returns a SmartButtonStats object containing both aggregates and
a per-button breakdown list.

UIManagerService.EmitBuildUIPerfLines emits the expanded line plus
one DEBUG line per SmartButton with its compile/execute/invoke split.

New log shape:
  [PERF]   pyRevitCore/SmartButton: engineInit=9ms, compile=3ms, execute=2615ms, invoke=51ms (x3)
  [PERF]     'Update':     compile=0ms, execute=2018ms, invoke=47ms
  [PERF]     'Extensions': compile=1ms, execute= 340ms, invoke= 2ms
  [PERF]     'Settings':   compile=2ms, execute= 257ms, invoke= 2ms

Add Python-side [PERF:py] sidecar instrumentation

Adds a self-contained pyrevit/_perf.py helper that emits DEBUG [PERF:py]
lines to the per-process csharp_loader.log sidecar (the same file the C#
LoggingHelper writes to when [core] csharp_filelogging = true). Format
mirrors the C# [PERF] lines for visual parity in the interleaved log:

  DEBUG [PERF:py] <label>: <N>ms             (mark checkpoint)

The helper is stdlib-only so it can be imported as the very first line

Runtime:
- Guard re-entrant render pumping (ScriptConsole.ForceRenderFrame) and
  buffered flushing (ScriptIO) with thread-level flags. Output windows
  share the UI dispatcher, so a pump triggered mid-render/flush could
  run another window's queued work and recurse until the native stack
  overflowed.

  recursion raises a catchable error instead of overflowing the stack

perf: cache attachment lookup and fix redundant disk scans

PyRevitAttachments.GetAttached() re-reads the addin manifests and the
clones registry from disk on every call, but the attachment Revit
launched with cannot change for the running session. This lookup sits
on the hot path of every script-engine spin-up: pyrevit.runtime calls
get_active_cpython_engine() at module import, so every clean-engine
command, hook execution, and CPython engine init paid the full scan.

- add AttachmentCache in the Runtime: session-scoped cache stored in
  AppDomain data (same pattern as EnvDictionary) so all script engines
  share a single disk lookup; cleared by load_session() so a
  re-attached clone is picked up on pyRevit reload. Deliberately not
  inside pyRevitLabs.PyRevit, which is shared with the CLI where
  attachments are mutated and re-read within one invocation.
- route CPythonEngine.GetPythonDll() and
  userconfig.get_current_attachment() through the cache
- GetAllAttached(): enumerate the lazy attachment scan once instead of
  twice (Count() + ToList() each re-ran the full registry/manifest read)
- ScriptExecutor.Initialize(): no-op when already initialized; both the
  python and c# session managers call it during load, and recreating
  the ExternalEvent orphaned the previous registration

perf(loader): key assembly build fingerprint on version only

The assembly build fingerprint previously mixed in the loader DLL's
file write time alongside its version. The write time changes on every
local rebuild and CI redeploy, so the cache key changed on every load
and forced every extension assembly to be regenerated even when
nothing in the generator actually changed.
